SigVerify scheduler CPU with tag state machines, ROM fetch, and scratchpad memory.

# Purpose
This file defines the scheduler CPU used for Solana `SigVerify` processing in the Firedancer design. The main `shcl_cpu` module implements a multi-tag, instruction-driven control path that feeds a fixed-latency arithmetic pipeline in `ed25519_sigverify_ecc`. It uses a virtual address scheme, per-tag state machines, instruction fetch from `schl_cpu_instr_rom`, and separate data memories for 256-bit values and ternary selector bits. The design also loads constant values at startup, accepts input hashes in groups, tracks per-tag scratch memory, and writes results back after the ALU completes each operation.

The file also includes the `schl_pkg` package, which defines the scheduler state encoding, and a simulation top level `schl`. The top level adds a FIFO in front of the CPU input so testbench traffic can be buffered, then connects the CPU output to the external result ports. Overall, the file provides the full control and memory orchestration layer for the SigVerify runtime, while the math operations themselves are handled by the separate ALU module.
